A.depoimento: I ordered my legions to split and strike the neutral villages of Santarem and Evora simultaneously. With the spearmen leading the charge, we easily overpowered the sparse garrisons. Lisboa is also busy forging two new spearheads to reinforce our growing army.
A.plano: Capture Santarem and Evora this turn to expand to 3 villages. Next turn, build more troops from the newly captured villages and Lisboa, and push towards Coimbra and Faro to secure the north and south routes. Focus on spearmen for cheap, fast expansion and use archers/knights to counter local defenses.

B.depoimento: I have launched an assault on the neutral village of Tarragona to claim my second territory and boost my resource income. In the capital, I ordered the construction of two additional spearmen to maintain defense and prepare for future expansions.
B.plano: Capture the neutral village Tarragona [21] to expand my economy and secure a second village. Build 2 spearmen in Barcelona [22] to replenish the garrison. Next turn, evaluate Girona [23] and watch for any enemy movements.

A.depoimento: I have ordered the construction of 2 spearmen in Lisboa to bolster my forces. My armies from Santarem and Evora have marched to capture the neutral villages of Coimbra, Badajoz, and Faro. This will expand my territory to 6 villages and secure my borders. I expect victory and look forward to the next phase of my campaign.
A.plano: Capture Coimbra, Badajoz, and Faro this turn to expand to 6 villages. Next turn, build troops in Lisboa, Santarem, and Evora, and push towards Porto, Salamanca, and Sevilha to secure the north and south routes. Focus on spearmen for cheap expansion and use archers/knights to counter local defenses. Continue exploring the map to find the enemy.

A.depoimento: We are building up our forces and moving troops to the frontlines. Our spearman are gathering at Coimbra for the assault on Porto, while knights concentrate at Badajoz for the push into Toledo. We aim to expand our territory and secure new villages.
A.plano: Focus on the northern front to capture Porto. Move spearman from Santarem to Coimbra and from Lisboa to Santarem to build a spearman army. In the south, concentrate knights at Badajoz by sending the knight from Faro. Build a knight in Lisboa and spearman in Santarem and Evora. Next turn, attack Porto from Coimbra with spearman, and prepare to attack Toledo from Badajoz with knights. Continue building the economy and exploring once neutral villages are captured.

B.depoimento: King B orders the assault on the neutral villages! Barcelona's knights ride to Girona, while Tarragona's archers and spearmen march on Castellon and Zaragoza. The enemy will soon find our borders expanding!
B.plano: We are launching a major expansion this turn, attacking the three visible neutral villages (Girona, Castellon, Zaragoza) to secure territory and increase our resource production. Barcelona will send a strong force to Girona, while Tarragona will split its forces to take Castellon and Zaragoza. We will also build an archer in Tarragona and a knight in Barcelona to grow our army. Next turn, we must consolidate our new villages and explore the map further.

A.depoimento: The king's armies strike! Porto and Toledo fall to our spearman and knights. We build spearman in every village and send reinforcements to the front. The campaign advances!
A.plano: Capture Porto and Toledo this turn to reach 8 villages. Next turn, build up Coimbra and Badajoz with reinforcements. Then attack Salamanca from Coimbra with spearman, and Sevilha from Badajoz with a mix of spearman and knights. Explore the unexplored villages to the north and east. Continue building spearman in all villages to maintain momentum.

B.depoimento: Turn 4: I am launching attacks on Huesca and Pamplona to expand my territory. My forces in Girona and Zaragoza are on the march. I am also building new knights and archers in my core villages to strengthen my army. The conquest of these villages will bring me closer to victory.
B.plano:
Attack Huesca (from Girona) and Pamplona (from Zaragoza) to expand territory.
Build knights and archers in Barcelona and Tarragona to grow the army.
Next turn: consolidate Huesca, wait for Pamplona, explore north via Pamplona, prepare for Madrid or other targets.

A.depoimento: This turn, we focused on reinforcing our armies. We sent a knight from Santarem to Coimbra, spearman from Faro and Santarem to Badajoz, and archers from Badajoz to Toledo. Our builders worked tirelessly, producing knights in Coimbra and Santarem, and spearman in Lisboa, Evora, Badajoz, and Faro. We are preparing for a major push!
A.plano: This turn we build up our armies for upcoming attacks. We send a knight from Santarem to Coimbra and build a knight there to prepare an attack on Salamanca. We send spearman from Faro and Santarem to Badajoz and build spearman there to prepare an attack on Sevilha. We also send archers from Badajoz to Toledo to prepare for an attack on Cordoba. Next turn, we will launch these attacks and continue expanding east toward the enemy capital.

B.depoimento: I am building up my army across my villages, focusing on knights in Barcelona and archers in Tarragona. I am sending reinforcements from Huesca to Pamplona to ensure the victory of the marching army and secure the northern expansion.
B.plano: Build knights and archers in Barcelona and Tarragona, spearmen in Castellon and Zaragoza. Send reinforcements from Huesca to Pamplona to secure its capture. Wait for the Zaragoza army to arrive and conquer Pamplona, then explore north.

A.depoimento: King A's armies advance! Knights from Coimbra strike Salamanca, archers from Toledo assault Cordoba, and spearmen from Badajoz march on Sevilha. Reinforcements from Faro secure Badajoz. The campaign to expand our territory has begun!
A.plano: This turn we launch a three-pronged attack: Coimbra's knights take Salamanca, Toledo's archers and knight take Cordoba, and Badajoz's spearmen take Sevilha. We also send spearmen from Faro to reinforce Badajoz. After capturing these villages, we will use Salamanca to attack Madrid, and Cordoba to attack Murcia. We will continue building troops in all villages to sustain the campaign. Our goal is to expand eastwards, capture neutral villages, and eventually hold 18 villages to secure victory.

B.depoimento: We are consolidating our position in the north. Reinforcements are heading to Pamplona to secure our hold and prepare for the assault on Burgos. Our economy is growing as we train more troops.
B.plano: Reinforce Pamplona with spearmen from Huesca and Zaragoza. Build knights and spearmen in all available villages to prepare for the attack on Burgos next turn. Do not attack Valencia yet as we lack the numbers.

A.depoimento: This turn we are massing our forces for a decisive push. We have sent knights to reinforce Salamanca and Badajoz, and spearmen to Porto, Cordoba, and Sevilha. Our armies are in position to capture four villages next turn, bringing us closer to our goal of 18 villages. The enemy remains unseen, but we are prepared.
A.plano: Our campaign continues with a multi-pronged expansion. This turn we are reinforcing our forward villages: sending a knight from Coimbra to Salamanca, spearmen from Coimbra to Porto and from Porto to Salamanca, spearmen from Toledo to Cordoba, and knights from Santarem to Badajoz. We also send spearmen from Badajoz to Sevilha to join the attack. Next turn, we will launch attacks on Madrid from Salamanca, Vigo from Porto, Murcia from Cordoba, and Sevilha will fall to our existing army. After capturing these, we will have 14 villages and will push further east to capture Teruel and the remaining

A.depoimento: I have ordered a bold three-pronged assault on the neutral villages of Vigo, Madrid, and Murcia. My armies are marching now, and I expect to conquer them next turn. I am also reinforcing my forward positions and building up my knight forces to break through the enemy's defenses. The path to Barcelona is opening, and I will not rest until the enemy capital falls.
A.plano: Our campaign is shifting to a multi-front expansion. This turn we attack Vigo, Madrid, and Murcia to increase our village count to 14. We are sending spearman from Porto to Vigo, knights from Salamanca to Madrid, and a mixed force from Cordoba to Murcia. We are also reinforcing Sevilha from Badajoz, sending knights to Toledo to prepare for the attack on Teruel, and reinforcing Porto and Salamanca from Coimbra for the next pushes. After capturing these neutral villages, we will have 14 villages and will push further east to capture Burgos, Zaragoza, Valencia, and Teruel, aiming to reach 18 vill

B.depoimento: I am launching a double attack on Valencia and Burgos to secure key northern territories. I am sending all available troops to these targets, while reinforcing my core villages to prevent any counter-attacks. My northern empire is expanding!
B.plano: Attack Valencia and Burgos to expand territory. Reinforce Castellon, Pamplona, Barcelona, and Zaragoza with remaining troops. Build spearman in all villages to maintain garrisons. Aim to secure the northern cluster and push south towards Madrid and Teruel next turns.

A.depoimento: This turn we strengthen our defenses by sending troops from Porto to Vigo, Salamanca and Badajoz to Madrid, and Cordoba and Sevilha to Murcia. We also order an attack on Teruel with knights and spearmen from Toledo. Meanwhile, we produce archers in all our interior villages to build up our army for the next pushes. We expect to capture Teruel next turn and continue our expansion.
A.plano: Our campaign is shifting to a multi-front expansion. This turn we reinforce our border villages (Vigo, Madrid, Murcia) from interior villages, and launch an attack on the neutral village Teruel using knights and spearmen from Toledo. We also build archers in all interior villages to prepare for attacks on enemy villages (Burgos, Zaragoza, Valencia) next turn. After capturing Teruel, we will have 15 villages and will push further east to capture Burgos, Zaragoza, and Valencia, aiming to reach 18 villages and secure victory.

A.depoimento: This turn we focused on reinforcement and building. We sent available troops from interior villages to our borders, and we built archers in nearly all our villages. We did not attack, as we want to gather sufficient forces first. Our borders are now stronger, and we prepare to strike at the enemy next turn.
A.plano: Our campaign is shifting to a multi-front expansion. This turn we reinforce our border villages (Madrid, Teruel, Murcia, Vigo) from interior villages, and build archers in all capable villages. We do not attack this turn, as we wait for reinforcements to arrive. Next turn, we will launch attacks on Burgos from Madrid, Valencia from Teruel, and Zaragoza from Madrid or Teruel. Our goal is to reach 18 villages and secure victory.

B.depoimento: I have ordered a full attack on Teruel with Castellon's army, hoping to conquer our 10th village. I am also reinforcing Castellon with Tarragona's archers and Tarragona with Barcelona's spearman to maintain a strong defense line. All my villages are producing troops to grow our forces for the next campaign.
B.plano: Our goal is to hold 18 villages. We currently hold 9. Teruel [13] is the weakest enemy village (defense 10). I will attack it with Castellon's full army to conquer it. To secure the border, I will send Tarragona's archers to reinforce Castellon, and Barcelona's spearman to reinforce Tarragona. All villages are building troops to prepare for the next expansion.

A.depoimento: This turn we built archers across our empire and moved reinforcements to the front. Our forces are gathering at Madrid and Murcia to strike Burgos and Valencia next turn. We also strengthened Vigo and other border villages. The enemy is attacking Teruel, and we hope our defenders can hold the line. We are one step closer to capturing 18 villages and winning the war.
A.plano: Our campaign is focusing on a dual offensive next turn. We are building archers in all villages and moving them to the borders. We will attack Burgos from Madrid and Valencia from Murcia with concentrated archer forces. We also reinforce Vigo and other borders for defense. The enemy is attacking Teruel; we hope our garrison there holds. After capturing these two, we will have 17 villages and need one more to reach 18. We will then target Zaragoza or another nearby village.

B.depoimento: Turn 11: We launch a massive assault on Teruel, the enemy's weakest border. Every available troop from our nearby villages is ordered to converge on the target. Castellon's second army, Valencia, Zaragoza, and reinforcements from the north will hit the enemy in successive waves. We aim to shatter their defense, capture the village, and open a path to the enemy heartland.
B.plano: Focus all might on capturing Teruel [13]. First wave (Turn 12): 4 armies from Castellon (x2), Valencia, Zaragoza. Second wave (Turn 13-14): Pamplona, Huesca, Tarragona, Barcelona. Left minimal garrisons in border villages; they are stripped intentionally. Build replacements now. After Teruel, expand to Madrid/Murcia. Do not attack our temporarily weak villages.

A.depoimento: King A orders a swift strike on the weak enemy villages of Zaragoza and Valencia while the enemy is focused on Teruel. Our armies march to conquer these lands, and we quietly build up our forces for the next battle at Burgos. The enemy will find us ready.
A.plano: Our campaign focuses on exploiting the enemy's distraction at Teruel. This turn, we attack Zaragoza from Madrid and Valencia from Murcia with overwhelming force. We reinforce Vigo from Porto and build archers to prepare for the attack on Burgos next turn. We also move troops from interior villages to borders (Badajoz to Toledo, Santarem to Badajoz, Cordoba to Murcia) to strengthen our positions. After capturing Zaragoza and Valencia, we will have 16 villages. Next turn, we will attack Burgos from Vigo and continue pushing toward the enemy capital, Barcelona.

B.depoimento: Turn 13: We have successfully captured Teruel! All marching armies are arriving this turn to reinforce our new border. I am sending local villages to bolster Teruel's garrison and building up our forces across the realm. Next turn, we will strike at Toledo with overwhelming force.
B.plano: Reinforce Teruel [13] with troops from Valencia, Castellon, Pamplona, Huesca, Tarragona. Build archers and knights in all villages. Wait for the massive reinforcements to arrive at Teruel this turn, then launch a full-scale attack on Toledo [8] next turn. Do not attack Madrid or Vigo yet; focus on the weakest enemy border first.

A.depoimento: King A orders a massive multi-pronged offensive! Knights and archers strike at Castellon, Pamplona, Huesca, and Tarragona, while the Vigo army crushes Burgos. Reinforcements flow from the interior to the borders to secure our gains. The enemy's outer ring collapses!
A.plano: Our campaign focuses on exploiting the enemy's weak border villages. This turn, we attack Castellon, Pamplona, Huesca, and Tarragona with knights and archers from Valencia and Zaragoza, while Vigo launches a full assault on Burgos. We also reinforce our border villages (Toledo, Valencia, Vigo, Madrid) from our interior villages to prepare for the next turn. After capturing these 5 villages, we will hold 21 villages, securing a decisive victory.

B.depoimento: I am launching a massive pincer movement! The main army from Teruel is marching on Zaragoza, while Burgos strikes at Madrid. I am reinforcing my borders and building new knights to maintain the momentum. If these attacks succeed, I will finally break the enemy's hold on the central plains and open the road to the south. The fate of the kingdom hangs in the balance, but my troops are ready for victory!
B.plano: Launch a double offensive: Teruel [13] attacks Zaragoza [17] with the main army (31 spearman, 8 archer, 4 knight) to cut the enemy's central hub. Burgos [14] attacks Madrid [12] (7 spearman, 1 archer, 2 knight) to secure a weak border village and open a southern route. Reinforce Tarragona [21] with troops from Barcelona [22] and send the Tarragona archer to Barcelona to balance the defense. Build knights in all major villages and spearmen in Teruel and Burgos to sustain the offensive. Do not attack Valencia or Toledo yet; consolidate gains first.

A.depoimento: This turn, we stand fast at Zaragoza, bringing in reinforcements from Madrid to hold the line. Our Toledo army strikes hard at Teruel, aiming to break the enemy's backbone. A lone knight from Pamplona seizes Huesca. Across the realm, we build knights in every village and shuffle our reserves toward the border, ready for the next push.
A.plano: Defend Zaragoza against the enemy counter-attack by reinforcing from Madrid. Launch a major assault on Teruel from Toledo to eliminate the enemy's main force. Capture Huesca with a knight from Pamplona. Build knights in all villages to expand our army. Move reserves from the interior to the front: Burgos to Pamplona, Badajoz to Toledo, and a pipeline from the west. After securing these victories, we will push on Tarragona and the enemy capital.

B.depoimento: Turn 14: I am launching a coordinated offensive on multiple fronts. Tarragona's army is sent to conquer Castellon, while Huesca's forces march on Pamplona. Barcelona and Girona send reinforcements to secure these border villages. Meanwhile, the main army from Teruel, along with the home garrison, is poised to conquer Zaragoza, the key to uniting my territories. I am building a mix of spearman, archers, and knights to sustain the momentum.
B.plano: Conquer Castellon [18] and Pamplona [19] to expand territory. Reinforce Tarragona and Huesca with Barcelona and Girona troops. Send Teruel home troops to Zaragoza [17] to secure the central hub after the main army conquers it. Focus on building spearman and archers to maintain garrisons.

A.depoimento: We reinforce our borders heavily this turn, sending thousands of troops to Madrid, Pamplona, Valencia, and Teruel to lock down our 18 villages. Our builders work overtime, producing knights in every single village. We are building an unbreakable wall to secure our empire and prepare for the final push next turn.
A.plano: This turn, we focus entirely on reinforcing our borders to secure our 18 villages. We send massive reinforcements from Toledo, Burgos, Salamanca, Teruel, and Murcia to Madrid, Pamplona, Valencia, and Teruel, making them impregnable. We also build knights in all our villages to expand our army. By holding our 18 villages this turn and next, we will secure victory. Next turn, we will launch coordinated attacks on Castellon and Huesca to eliminate the enemy's presence.

B.depoimento: I am sending a strike force from Zaragoza to conquer the weakly defended Madrid, expanding my territory. I am reinforcing my border villages of Castellon and Huesca, as well as the interior hub of Tarragona, to prepare for future campaigns. My villages are busy building spearmen and archers to replenish losses and grow my forces.
B.plano: Conquer Madrid [12] with troops from Zaragoza to expand territory. Reinforce Castellon [18] from Tarragona, Huesca [20] from Girona, and Tarragona [21] from Barcelona to secure borders. Build spearmen and archers in all villages to grow the army. Do not attack Teruel [13] or Valencia [16] yet as they are too well defended.
